title: Component library: the ISO30 holder entries are not built-in components

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: P7

body:
**Problem.** The built-in component library (#3645, merged in #4233) does not contain the `ISO30` holder entries of the holder library.

`component_library::builtin_holders` parses the taper name with `ConnectionCode::parse`. `ISO30` is not a connection code, so the conversion skips each `ISO30` entry without a message.

The holder library defines `ISO30` as the router name of DIN 69871 size 30, with the same steel as `SK30` (`crates/tools/src/holder_library_din.rs`, `pub const ISO30: Taper = Taper { name: "ISO30", ..SK30 }`).

**Effect.** A router user cannot select an `ISO30` holder from the built-in components. The user must draw the holder by hand. No wrong output: the entry is missing, not wrong.

**Done means.**
- Decide how `ISO30` maps: an alias of `SK30` in `ConnectionCode::parse`, or a separate code that mates only `ISO30`. Record the decision in `docs/decisions/`.
- The `ISO30` entries are built-in components.
- Remove the `ISO30` exception from the test `every_holder_with_a_taper_is_a_built_in_and_a_shrink_fit_bore_is_plain` in `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/builtin_shrink.rs` (PR #4251).

Found during the review fix of PR #4251. The effort is `effort:high` because built-in holder outlines feed the collision checks (safety floor).

body:
The research for #4145 recommends ISO dialect M for the existing 840D post. The post currently mixes ISO drilling with native Siemens output.

Research and sources: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/4145#issuecomment-7210769858

Implement the smallest useful slice:

- Emit `G291` in a separate block before executable setup commands.
- State the ISO dialect M requirement. Do not assume that G291 selects milling instead of turning.
- Use ISO unit words. Check the start and end of the program. Do not change units with active offsets without the required sequence.
- Use the ISO work-offset scheme for offsets 1-6. Check the physical frame mapping. Update the displayed names and explanations.
- Activate valid ISO tool length before motion. Use a stated machine mapping for the ISO offset numbers. Refuse an unknown mapping.
- State the cycle return mode. Preserve the existing seating and clearance rules.
- Keep `G83 P<ms>` by the maintainer decision in #2349. Keep the existing G73, G84, G85 and G86 dwell refusals.
- Give control compensation, control rotation, probing and smoothing valid ISO output or a named refusal. A refusal must block program release.
- Check the full program for native commands that ISO mode does not permit.

A Siemens subprogram call can be legal in ISO mode. Do not reject `CYCLE832(...)` only because its name is Siemens-specific. Check the installed cycle contract before support is claimed.

Use complete-program tests. Cover both units, offsets 1-6, tool changes, first motion, drilling, section changes and program end. Test each feature that can request native output. Keep the G83 dwell regression.

Code context:

- `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:317-330`: program opening.
- `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:356-398`: control compensation and offset names.
- `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:450-560`: smoothing, units, tools, rotation and section end.
- `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:685-795`: drilling.
- `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:803-944`: probing and program end.
- `crates/post/src/post/engine.rs:359-389`: cycle dispatch.
- `crates/post/tests/sinumerik_g83_dwell.rs`: the verified dwell interface.

Coordinate with #4143 for tool offsets, #4144 for retracts, and #4150 for G94. Do not duplicate their fixes.

Done means: Complete-program tests prove one explicit ISO language, valid units and offsets, correct tool length and drilling, and named refusals for unsupported features. G83 retains `P<ms>`. Each refusal blocks program release.

Priority: P7 is the implementation follow-up within the requested research range. The umbrella keeps P3.

Effort: high. The safety floor applies because this work changes posted G-code and refusal behavior.

body:
## What happens

1. `grbl.cps` and `grblhal.cps` always start the spindle with `S.. M3`. The posts do not declare `millSpindleReverse`. The engine asks for a reverse spindle with `PARAM MillSpindle reverse` (`crates/post/src/post/mod.rs:266-279`), and a post without the flag refuses that section by name. Thus a legal program (for example, a left-hand cutter) is refused on these posts.
2. The program header does not cancel `G92` offsets. A `G92` offset from an earlier job stays active on the control.

These refusals are safe. The posts make no wrong output.

## Expected

1. The two posts declare `millSpindleReverse = true`. They read `PARAM MillSpindle` and write `M4` for a reverse section, as `fanuc.cps` does.
   - Grbl 1.1 needs a spindle direction output for `M4`. On a board without that output, `M4` turns the spindle clockwise. Thus `grbl.cps` writes `M4` only when the machine file states a spindle direction output. If it does not, the post keeps the refusal by name.
2. A post option (default off) writes `G92.1` in the header of the two posts. The default stays off because some grbl senders set work zero with `G92`. On those machines, `G92.1` removes the work zero of the operator.

## Evidence

Main `8937e684d`:

- `assets/posts/grbl.cps:480` and `assets/posts/grblhal.cps:476`: `block(["S" + ni(sRpm), "M3"])`. Neither post declares `millSpindleReverse`.
- `assets/posts/fanuc.cps:23`, `:676`, `:824`: the `millSpindleReverse` pattern.
- `assets/posts/grbl.cps:346` and `assets/posts/grblhal.cps:334`: the header block has no `G92.1`.
- Sources: the Grbl v1.1 and grblHAL G-code references (M3/M4, G92/G92.1).
- Related: #4102 (left-hand cutter runs M4 on the posts that have the flag), #4151 (`G92.1` for `linuxcnc.cps` only), #714 (grblHAL 4th axis, not in this scope).

Found by the post audit against the Grbl and grblHAL manuals (#4130).

## Done means

- `grblhal.cps` writes `M4` for a reverse section. A posted-G-code test pins it.
- `grbl.cps` writes `M4` only when the machine file states a spindle direction output. If it does not, the post refuses by name. Tests pin the two cases.
- With the option on, the two posts write `G92.1` in the header. With the option off, the output does not change. Tests pin the two cases.

title: Comprehensive feeds and speeds calculator using machine, tool, and stock material limits

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
### What are you trying to do

When setting up a new toolpath, I want to calculate reliable RPM (`S`) and feed rates (`F`) directly inside CamCraft based on my specific mill, cutter, and workpiece material. 

Right now, CamCraft only provides basic baseline lookup windows per material without accounting for machine spindle limits, tool geometry, or stepover/stepdown engagement. Because of this, I have to leave CamCraft to calculate safe parameters in external tools—especially when working on lighter-duty or benchtop mills where spindle torque, max RPM, and tool deflection are major constraints—and manually copy those numbers back into every operation.

### How you imagine it working

Expand the cutting data panel and tool library with an integrated calculator that pulls from the active setup:

1. **Machine profile (`.mch`):** Factor in the machine's min/max spindle RPM, spindle power/torque limits, and maximum cutting feed rates.
2. **Tool parameters:** Account for cutter diameter, number of flutes, tool material/coating (HSS vs. uncoated/coated carbide), and flute length / stickout.
3. **Stock material & engagement:** Use the selected workpiece material along with the operation's radial stepover ($a_e$) and axial depth of cut ($a_p$) to automatically apply radial chip-thinning compensation.

From those inputs, CamCraft would suggest optimal RPM, chip load ($f_z$), cutting feed rate, and plunge rate with one click to apply them to the operation—and display a clear warning if the calculated cut exceeds the machine's power/RPM limits or risks excessive tool deflection.

title: Dynamic feed-rate optimization based on remaining in-process stock

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
### What are you trying to do

When machining a part across multiple operations (such as roughing followed by rest machining, semi-finishing, or finishing), later operations frequently cut areas where most of the stock has already been removed. 

Today, CamCraft applies a single static feed rate to the entire operation. This means the tool crawls at full-engagement speeds even when it is only taking a light clean-up pass or experiencing radial chip thinning, wasting cycle time and causing the cutter to rub instead of shear.

### How you imagine it working

CamCraft already tracks the in-process stock (IPW) between operations, so it could use that remaining stock model to scale the linear feed rate (`F`) per toolpath segment based on actual radial and axial engagement:

- **Scale feed up on light cuts:** When the actual radial width of cut ($a_e$) is smaller than the nominal stepover—such as when entering a previously cleared pocket—automatically increase the feed rate to compensate for radial chip thinning and keep the chip load consistent, up to a user-defined maximum multiplier or machine ceiling.
- **Slow down in tight corners:** Reduce the feed rate automatically when the cutter enters high-engagement zones or sharp internal corners where wrap angle spikes.
- **Per-operation controls:** Add a toggle in the operation's cutting data panel to enable feed optimization, set min/max feed scaling limits, and preview the resulting feed-rate heat map in the toolpath simulation.

The kernel gives a `Plan` (entries, cuts, links, lifts, the exit). No production code turns a `Plan` into a `Toolpath`. Add the converter in `camcraft-motion`:

In the simulation playback of a rotary program (a rotary that turns the work about a horizontal line, e.g. a Rotary Flow on a mill-turn with an A rotary), an indexed/posed station is drawn with the whole tool assembly - shank, holder, spindle housing - rotating about the TOOL TIP, while the work stays at its document pose. The tool visibly swings from radial to pointing down, driving the 250 mm housing far below the table.

The playback timeline carries only a tool tip and a tool-axis vector (`crates/sim/src/sim.rs:188-218`, `:602-632` - a posed move is stored as an A/B/C letter, never a work transform), and the renderer poses the tool about the tip with a shortest-rotation map (`crates/app/src/tool_body_view.rs:151-177`), reading no rotary axis line (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/world.rs:313-348`).

## Why it matters

The drawn motion is kinematically wrong for a work-turning rotary: the machine turns the WORK about the rotary line while the tool stays upright. The playback shows the opposite, which reads as a collision that does not exist and hides the one that could. Display-only today (the post gate runs its own math), but it trains the user's eye on the wrong kinematics.

## Suggested behaviour

At an indexed pose, draw the work rotated about the stated rotary axis line and the tool upright (or at minimum, draw the tool upright at the tip station and note the simplification), matching the machine-frame kinematics the gate judges with.

Suggested labels: P7, area:ui, effort:medium, source:agent.

body:
﻿## What happens

A Rotary Flow operation on a part mounted along the machine X axis, machined on a Doosan DNM 5700 + rotary table (A, turns the work), is refused at post with:

```
Flow1: spindle housing at move 3 strikes a fixture
Flow1: spindle housing at move 99 strikes a fixture
```

The reporter states no fixture and no workholding beyond the machine table. The only "fixture" in the judged set is the machine-derived table (`MACHINE_TABLE`, folded into the fixture boxes). Moves 3 and 99 are early approach/link moves, not deep cuts.

## The kinematic question

The rotary table turns the WORK; the table steel is fixed in the machine frame. The spindle housing only reaches the table's Z band if the tool descends beside the part into it - at approach/link stations with a normal stick-out, a housing-table strike is surprising. Two candidate explanations:

1. A frame bug: the housing pose or the table box is judged in the wrong frame at an indexed pose (the table box rotated with the part's frame, or the housing pose not transformed into the machine frame), so the check refuses a legal program.
2. A real catch: the holder is short, the A index deep (-86.250 deg), and the housing genuinely enters the table's swept band at those stations.

The reporter believes (1): "the table rotary turns, but the table doesn't - so the tool can't hit the table unless it goes way down in Z."

## Reproduction

Small cylinder (R 9, 30 long) mounted along X, stock 30 x 44 x 44, Rotary Flow with a 3 mm ball, nose-to-axis stated on the setup, post to the Doosan DNM 5700 + rotary table. The refusal names moves 3 and 99. The project file is available from the reporter.

## What the fix should settle

- Which frame the housing band and the fixed table box are judged in at an indexed pose.
- Whether the refused poses are legal (the refusal is phantom) or the finding is real and the message should say WHICH steel was struck (it names no box today - "a fixture" for a user with no fixture reads as a bug).

body:
Part of #4023. Follow-up of #4241 (PR #4253) and of K4 (#4177). It is delivered on `side/path-kernel` (AGENTS.md **Side branch**).

## What happens

For the material side Outside, the kernel plan lifts 13 times on the disc band and 15 times on the dog-bone band. Each lift has a named reason. The design record (K0, #4024) has the target of 0 lifts on the disc, and the old 2D Offset planner has 0 there.

PR #4253 lets a link run in the band outside the stock and along the air. The lifts stay, because the last stretch is not proved: the way from the air back in to the start of the next piece. Each of those starts is more than 0.9 tool radius from each finished cut, so the link would go over uncut stock.

## What to do

The design record decided for #3934 that the split pieces of an Outside band are joined as the Adaptive air plan joins them. Apply that to the last stretch:

- Each ring that is cut open at the stock edge has its two ends on the stock outline. The order stage can start such a piece at an end that the air reaches.
- The approach from the air to that end is an entry in air in the cut plane (law 5): the tool comes from the air and starts to cut along the planned curve. It does not go over uncut stock off a curve. Prove the approach with the proof of the entry stage (the lead-in of an air entry), not with a new assumption.
- A piece whose ends are not at the stock edge keeps the present rule. If no proved way exists, the lift stays and has its named reason.
- Do not make a strip of uncut stock "open" by a constant. The review of PR #4234 found that defect one time.

## Pins

- Negative tests first: an approach from the air that would cut uncut stock off the curve is refused; an approach near a keep-out at the stock edge is refused; an approach beside a part that reaches out of the stock is refused.
- The law suite (`order_link::k4_link_rule_holds_and_each_lift_is_named`) and the motion pin (`kernel_order_and_link_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone`) are measured again, with no tuning of a constant. Give the counts as measured. For each lift that stays on the disc, say which link has no proof and why.
- Inside and Outside still cut the same curves (law 3). 0 crossing feeds.

## Done means

The Outside lift counts on the disc band and the dog-bone band are measured again with the proved approach, each lift that stays has its named reason, and the pins are green. If the count on the disc is not 0, the PR says exactly what blocks it.

body:
## Summary

This issue is a proposal from the two UI owners. It shows the target workspace in two mockups. It also gives the plan: the issues and pull requests that we intend to make, and the release order.

We ask the maintainer to read it and to answer the questions at the end. We do not file the sub-issues before the maintainer answers.

## Goal and limits

- CamCraft must feel like a CAM tool. A person who knows a CAM system must find the setup tree, the operation properties, Generate, Simulate and Post without a manual.
- The workspace must work on a small screen. Each side pane folds, so the viewport gets more space.
- No change in this plan changes a toolpath or posted G-code. The UI pull requests change only the look, the layout and the messages.
- Each change from the UI stays an undoable command. The MCP tools stay the same.
- Clean room: the mockups are our own drawings. We used no text, icons, layout or screenshots from another CAM product.

## Mockups

Both mockups are 1366 × 768. The source file is a FigCraft file in our design notes. They use the design language of research note 3: flat docked panes, neutral grey with a blue accent, IBM Plex Sans and IBM Plex Mono (SIL OFL), and the CamCraft icons from `assets/ui/`.

### E1: all panes open

![E1: all panes open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/ui-proposal-images/ui-proposal/E1-proposal.png)

- Title bar: menu bar, Save, Undo and Redo, and document tabs. The second tab shows the target. Until CamCraft can open more than one file, there is one tab. The magnifier is a placeholder for a command search.
- Ribbon: a machine-mode list ("Milling") and workflow tabs in program order: Setup, 2D, 3D, Drill, Multi-axis, Simulate, Post. The ribbon shows only the groups of the selected tab.
- Browser: the setup first (stock, machine, then the operations in program order). Each operation shows its state as a symbol and a word: current, never, calculating (elapsed time), stale, failed. "Machine: not set · Choose…" is a warning that you can click.
- Viewport: the height planes have a key with the name of the operation, and labels in the scene.
- Properties: the operation editor has six groups: Tool and cutting data, Geometry, Heights, Passes, Entry and linking, Accuracy and output. A folded group shows its values on one line. Each height shows its reference, its offset and the result: "= Z 10.000 in G54". A small text tag shows the source of each value: default, template, derived or set. A disabled button tells why it is disabled. Delete is in the ⋯ menu.
- Issues pane, below the viewport: each issue names its cause and has one button that goes to the fix. A check that did not run shows as "unavailable", never as "passed". The running job shows its elapsed time and Cancel.

### E2: all panes folded

![E2: all panes folded](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/ui-proposal-images/ui-proposal/E2-proposal-folded.png)

- A folded side pane becomes a title chip on the viewport. The viewport then uses the full width. A click on a chip opens the pane again. The camera does not move when a pane folds or opens.
- Each chip keeps the safety state as text. The Browser chip shows the counts of failed and stale operations. The Properties chip shows the state of the operation.
- The issues pane folds to one line. The line keeps the counts and the running job with Cancel.
- The move-type key lists only the move types that the project contains. A hover tag on a move shows the operation, the move type and the feed rate.

Parts of E1 and E2 need engine work first: the source badges, the "failed" state, and a stop inside the generators. The section "Plan, step 2" names them.

## What CamCraft has today

We checked the code on `main`:

- Heights already have a reference and an offset (`HeightReference` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/height.rs`). The UI can show the result now.
- An operation has three states: Never, Ok and Stale (`OpStatus` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/sel.rs`).
- The windowed app generates toolpaths on a worker thread, with a progress overlay and Cancel (#2257). Cancel discards the result, but the worker continues to the end.
- The toolpath data has three move kinds: Rapid, Feed and Plunge (`crates/cl/src/cl/moves.rs`).
- CamCraft opens one project at a time.

## Plan, step 0: the UI kit crate

The maintainer asked on Discord to collect the UI/UX work into a crate. We propose a new crate `crates/ui-kit` (`camcraft-ui-kit`) for the design system.

- The crate depends on `egui` only. It does not depend on `camcraft-app`.
- It holds the tokens and the theme: colour roles, sizes, the theme-file reader and the contrast checks.
- It holds the components:
  - the pane frame, which folds to a title chip;
  - the title chips;
  - the ribbon cell and its groups;
  - the form row with units, the source badge and the result line;
  - the folded group with its summary line;
  - the status card for never, current, stale, calculating and failed;
  - the action band with the reasons for disabled buttons;
  - the keys for the heights and the move types;
  - the issue row.
- Each component takes plain data and returns the choice of the user. A component does not read the document. `crates/ui` keeps the panes. It changes the document into plain data, and it changes the choice into an undoable command.
- A small gallery binary shows each component in each state, in the light and the dark theme. Reviewers use it to compare the code with the mockups.

Why a crate:

1. The dependency graph makes the design rules true: a component cannot read the document, because the crate cannot see `camcraft-app`.
2. The crate compiles without flecs and the engine. Its tests (layout, contrast, AccessKit labels) run fast.
3. The look is in one place. A later palette (for example #655) maps onto one crate.

| PR | Content | Effort | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| K | Make the crate, with the decision entry for the new crate edge `ui → ui-kit` (AGENTS.md "No new dependency between our crates without a decision"). Move the theme tokens into it. Add the gallery binary. | high | R |

The later PRs build their components in the kit, and `crates/ui` keeps only the link to the app:

- B: form row, group, status card, action band.
- P: pane frame and title chips.
- D: ribbon cell.
- C1 and C2: the keys.
- I: the issue row.

We move existing code (the theme, the form seam) in the PR that touches it, never in one large move.

## Plan, step 1: UI work on what exists

These pull requests change no engine data. Each one is a `feat` PR in the enhancement lane, `P6`. Each one keeps toolpaths and posts the same, updates its `layout_page_*` and structural tests, and keeps the `crates/ui` test count (#1953).

| PR | Content | Effort | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|
| R | Refactor: split `panes.rs` (1665 lines) into ribbon, tabs and status bar files. No visible change. | medium | - |
| A | Theme: palette, a monospace font for numbers, the last colour literals into tokens (#1120, #4209). The tokens are in the kit. | medium | K |
| E | One command table and an in-app menu bar. The ribbon reads the same table. | high | R |
| D | Title bar with one document tab, the machine-mode list with workflow tabs, a ribbon that folds, status bar chips. All machine modes in one PR. | high | E |
| P | Side panes fold to title chips (components in the kit). The saved panel setups (#2339) keep the fold state. View ▸ Reset layout. | medium | R |
| C1 | Viewport (the keys are kit components): the heights key, plane labels in the scene, line patterns for the planes, the Display bar. | medium | A |
| C2 | The move-type key for the three move kinds, filtered to the project, and a hover tag on a move (operation · move type · feed). | medium | C1 |
| B | Pilot on the 2D Contour page: header, status card, height results, folded groups, disabled reasons, Delete in the ⋯ menu. Split `layout/form.rs` first (#1122). | high | A |
| B2 | The same frame on the other operation pages, one page family for each PR. | medium each | B |
| I | The issues pane, filled from the states that exist now: never generated, stale, refusals, no machine. | high | P |
| F | The Settings window of #3025, over the preference file. We use #3025 and do not file a new issue. | medium | E |

Each PR has a decision file in `docs/decisions/`. The first PR records the general UI decisions.

The Tier-1 UI rules go into `crates/ui/AGENTS.md` in a separate process PR (`Process change: yes`). The maintainer merges that PR.

## Plan, step 2: engine work

Each item is a design issue first (`P8`). We write a design note, and the maintainer accepts it before code starts. No item blocks step 1. When an item is done, a small UI PR shows its result.

| Item | Why it needs design | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| A real stop inside the generators, and a cancel tool for MCP | This is the open part of #3035 (see PR #4217). We do not file a new issue. We help on #3035. | max |
| Record why a toolpath is stale | The stamp is a hash. It knows that an input changed, but not which input. | high |
| A stored "failed" state | A new state for an operation. It can change the project file. | high |
| The source of each value (default, template, derived, set by the user) | Each parameter must store its source. This changes the project file. | max |
| More move kinds: ramp, lead-in and lead-out, link, finish pass | Each generator must mark its moves. This is under the safety floor. The posted G-code must not change. | max |
| More than one open project | One world and one undo history for each file. MCP tools must name the file. | max |

Later follow-ups: a command search (after E, `P7`), and a native macOS menu bar (after E; it needs a new dependency, so the maintainer decides).

## Release plan

`feat` PRs merge at a cut. We propose these groups. The maintainer decides the cut list.

| Cut | PRs | What a user sees |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | R, K, A, P, C1 | New colours, panes that fold, a better heights key. All commands stay where they are. |
| 2 | E, D, C2 | The menu bar, the new title bar and ribbon, the move-type key. This is the largest change, in one cut. |
| 3 | B and all B2, I | The new operation pages on all operations, and the issues pane. |
| 4 | F | The settings dialog. |

## The app stays usable during the rollout

- No PR changes the commands, the undo history, the MCP tools, the toolpaths or the posts. A person who tests CAM behaviour gets the same results at each step.
- B and all B2 PRs ship in the same cut. A user never sees half of the operation pages in the new layout.
- D changes the ribbon for all machine modes in one PR. E comes first, so each command is also in the menu bar.
- D and B update the user documentation for each command that moves.
- A folded pane always shows its title chip. View ▸ Reset layout opens all panes again.

## Related issues

- #655 (`P?`): we do not change it. This plan does not need the SolidCraft kit. Our token names stay our own, so a palette can map in later.
- #1120 and #1122: PR A and PR B do part of this work.
- #1953: each UI PR obeys this test plan.
- #2257: the worker for toolpath generation exists. E1 uses it.
- #3035 and PR #4217: the cancel and MCP part of step 2.
- #3025: PR F does this issue.
- #1677: the workbench rework. PR #1639 shipped it in v0.21.0: the `horizon-day` theme, the tab row for the machine modes, the compact Browser row and the section glyphs. It is on `main`. PR A, PR D and PR P start from this work and keep it. The issue is still open because the PR used `Refs #1677`.
- #2339: saved panel setups exist. PR P uses them for the fold state.
- #4209: PR A does this issue with #1120.
- #2261 (`P4`): direction arrows on toolpaths. PR C2 must not hide or change them.
- #661 (`P4`) and #659 (`P?`): an icon set and theme tokens in the style of SolidCraft, part of #655. This plan does not remove that work. Question 6 asks how the two directions fit together.

## Questions for the maintainer

1. Do you agree with the direction: a CAM tool first, panes that fold to title chips, and docked panes when they are open?
2. Minimum screen size: 1366 × 768, or 1280 × 800 at 150 % scale? The second is much smaller. At that size, not all panes can be open at the same time.
3. Do you agree with the in-app menu bar (PR E)?
4. Do you accept the engine items of step 2 as design issues? Three of them can change the project file.
5. Do you agree with the cut groups?
6. #661 asks for icons in the style of SolidCraft. This plan puts the CAM workflow first and keeps SolidCraft optional. Does #661 stay as it is, or does it follow this plan?
7. The UI kit crate: is a crate for the design system (tokens, theme and components, as in step 0) what you mean? Or do you want all UI code in crates, for example one crate for each pane family?

Done means: the maintainer answers the questions. Then we file the sub-issues of step 1 and step 2 and link them to this issue.

- `region_build::region` makes the cutter-centre area of an `Outside` region end at the stock outline.
- The air of the region starts one tool radius outside the stock (`s.offset(2r) - s.offset(r)`).
- A link sample between the stock outline and the air is in neither area. The link proof refuses it (`CUTS_PART`).
- After the fix of PR #4234, the strip just inside the stock edge is uncut stock until a cut clears it (`UNCUT_STOCK`).
- Thus the link from one piece at the stock edge to the next piece cannot stay down. The motion `kernel_laws` k4 pin reads 13 lifts on the disc band and 15 lifts on the dog-bone band (Outside). Each lift has a named reason. The old 2D Offset planner has 0 there.

The old ring links (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ring_links.rs`, `AIR`) let a link leave the stock: a centre outside the stock by 0.1 tool radius counts as air. Its tool then cuts at most 0.9 tool radius into the stock.

What to examine:
- A free band outside the stock where a link may run: outside the stock by 0.1 r or more, and away from the part by the tool radius plus the leave (the part can touch the stock edge).
- The proof that such a band cuts no part wall and no keep-out area.
- The new lift counts on the disc band and the dog-bone band.

Done means: the link proof can run a link through the proved band outside the stock. The lift counts of `order_link::k4_link_rule_holds_and_each_lift_is_named` and `kernel_order_and_link_round_the_disc_and_the_dog_bone` are measured again, and each remaining lift has its named reason.

title: 2D Contour: add integrated finish and spring passes

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
## Problem

2D Contour can leave stock for a later finishing operation.

A user must currently create and maintain another Contour operation to remove that stock. A spring pass needs another duplicated operation.

The duplicated operation repeats the geometry, lead settings, start point, exit point, heights, tabs and tool selection. A later change can make the rough and finish operations disagree.

## Proposal

Add an optional finish sequence to the 2D Contour operation.

The operator can create the complete rough and finish sequence in one operation. CamCraft keeps the current behavior when the option is off.

Add these controls to the Passes tab:

- `Stock to leave`
- `Finish in this operation`
- `Finish allowance`
- `Finishing passes`
- `Spring passes`

The proposed layout is:

```text
Stock to leave                 0.00 mm

☐ Finish in this operation
    Finish allowance           0.25 mm
    Finishing passes           1
    Spring passes              0
```

CamCraft hides the finish fields while `Finish in this operation` is off.

## Meaning of the values

`Stock to leave` remains the material that the complete operation leaves on the final wall.

`Finish allowance` is the additional material that the finishing passes remove.

`Finishing passes` divides the finish allowance across the finishing passes.

`Spring passes` repeats the final path without a new planned allowance.

Let:

- `S` be `Stock to leave`.
- `A` be `Finish allowance`.
- `N` be `Finishing passes`.

The rough pass uses this offset from the final wall:

```text
S + A
```

Finishing pass `i` uses this offset:

```text
S + A × (N - i) / N
```

The final finishing pass stands exactly at `S`.

Every spring pass also stands at `S`.

### Example

Use these values:

- `Stock to leave = 0.00 mm`
- `Finish allowance = 0.30 mm`
- `Finishing passes = 2`
- `Spring passes = 1`

CamCraft generates:

1. A rough pass at 0.30 mm from the final wall.
2. A finishing pass at 0.15 mm from the final wall.
3. A finishing pass on the final wall.
4. A spring pass on the final wall.

CamCraft applies the same formula to Inside and Outside contours.

A positive `Stock to leave` remains on the final wall after the complete sequence. The finishing passes remove only the `Finish allowance`.

## Default values

A new 2D Contour keeps `Finish in this operation` off.

When the operator enables it, CamCraft starts with:

- `Finish allowance = 0.25 mm`
- `Finishing passes = 1`
- `Spring passes = 0`

A disabled finish sequence generates the current toolpath.

A zero finish allowance is valid. One finishing pass can then repeat the final contour at a separate finish feed.

The proposed limits are:

- Finishing passes: 1 to 64.
- Spring passes: 0 to 4.

## Finish feed

Add an optional finish-feed override to the Feeds tab.

The proposed layout is:

```text
Feed                           1200 mm/min
Plunge feed                     300 mm/min

☐ Override finish feed
    Finish feed                1200 mm/min
```

The override follows these rules:

- It starts off.
- It copies the current `Feed` when the operator enables it.
- It keeps the entered value until the operator disables it.
- It stops inheriting `Feed` while the override is enabled.
- It uses `Feed` dynamically while the override is disabled.
- It uses the new current `Feed` after the operator disables and enables it again.
- Finishing passes and spring passes use the effective finish feed.
- Rough passes use `Feed`.
- The operation stores no separate finish spindle speed.

The operator does not need a separate feed for every pass.

## Feed behavior

The finish sequence uses these feed rules:

- The wall cut uses `Feed` for rough passes.
- The wall cut uses `Finish feed` for finishing and spring passes.
- A lead-in uses its existing lead-in percentage of the active wall feed.
- A lead-out uses the active wall feed.
- Plunge, ramp, helix and explicit entry-feed settings keep their current behavior.
- An automatic entry feed reads the active rough or finish wall feed.
- The spindle speed remains the same for the complete operation.

The finish-feed override must not modify the selected tool or its recipe.

## Existing lead-in and lead-out

The feature does not add a second lead editor.

Every rough, finishing and spring pass uses the operation's existing lead-in, lead-out, extension, overlap and compensation settings.

Each pass follows this sequence:

```text
safe approach → lead-in → wall pass → lead-out → safe retract
```

CamCraft recalculates the lead geometry for every radial offset.

CamCraft applies the existing room, crossing and collision checks to every recalculated lead.

The path must not move directly from one wall offset to another wall offset.

CamCraft retracts between offsets. It then enters the next pass with a new lead.

If the configured lead does not fit, CamCraft uses the existing lead refusal or shortening behavior. It must not silently plunge through the finished wall.

A spring pass repeats the complete final sequence, including lead-in, wall pass, lead-out and retract.

## Pass order

CamCraft completes each offset as a separate Contour band.

For each selected contour:

1. Complete the rough depth ladder at the rough offset.
2. Retract to a safe plane.
3. Complete the first finishing depth ladder.
4. Retract to a safe plane.
5. Complete each remaining finishing depth ladder.
6. Retract to a safe plane.
7. Repeat the final depth ladder for each spring pass.

The operation completes all rings and Z levels of one offset before it starts the next offset.

The existing level links apply inside one offset.

A keep-down link must not cross from one offset to another. CamCraft must use a safe lift between offset bands.

The current start point, exit point, compensation mode, tabs, corner rounding, overlap and entry settings apply to every offset band.

Control and wear compensation engage and cancel independently for every rough, finishing and spring band.

CamCraft retains all generated spring passes. A post or path optimizer must not remove a repeated final pass as a duplicate.

## Open contours and multiple selections

The feature applies to:

- Closed Contour rings.
- Open model-edge chains.
- Open stock-source runs.
- Multiple selected rings.
- Multiple disconnected runs.
- Multiple Z levels.
- Tabbed Contours.
- Inside and Outside sides.
- Computer, Wear and Control compensation.

Each run receives an independent lead-in and lead-out for every offset.

## Collision and verification

CamCraft applies the complete existing verification rules to every pass.

This includes:

- Model collision checks.
- Full cutter-envelope checks.
- Stock checks.
- Flute, shank and holder checks.
- Lead-room checks.
- Lead crossing checks.
- Keep-down link checks.
- Tab checks.
- Compensation checks.
- Open-chain air-side checks.

A finishing or spring pass must block posting when any check fails.

CamCraft must not use a rough path result as proof for a different offset.

## Validation

CamCraft refuses the operation before geometry generation when:

- `Stock to leave + Finish allowance` is negative or not finite.
- `Finish allowance` is negative or not finite.
- `Finishing passes` is outside its allowed range.
- `Spring passes` is outside its allowed range.
- An enabled finish-feed override is not positive and finite.
- The initial rough offset produces no legal cutter-centre path.
- A selected ring collapses at a finish or spring offset.

CamCraft identifies the invalid field and value in the refusal.

CamCraft must propagate a later unsafe finish or spring pass as an operation failure. It must not return a partial clean path.

## Project format

Add an optional finish record to the 2D Contour parameters.

The record contains:

- Finish allowance.
- Finishing-pass count.
- Spring-pass count.

Add an optional finish-feed value.

An absent finish record means that the feature is off.

An absent finish-feed value means that finishing uses the current `Feed`.

Existing project files retain the current Contour behavior.

A project that enables the feature round-trips every value through save and load.

Older project data must not acquire extra passes through a default value.

## UI behavior

All changes use the existing undoable operation-parameter command.

The Passes tab enables and disables the finish fields.

The Feeds tab enables and disables the finish-feed field.

Turning on the feed override copies the current `Feed` into `Finish feed`.

Turning off the feed override clears the override and restores inheritance.

Opening either tab must not modify the operation.

## MCP behavior

Expose the finish sequence through the 2D Contour MCP fields.

The MCP update must support:

- Enabling and disabling the finish sequence.
- Finish allowance.
- Finishing-pass count.
- Spring-pass count.
- Enabling and disabling finish-feed inheritance.
- Explicit finish feed.

An absent finish record keeps the old one-pass behavior.

The MCP schema and generated documentation must list the fields.

## Scope

This issue covers 2D Contour only.

Later issues can reuse the same model for:

- Bore.
- Circular.
- Slot.
- Trochoidal Slot.
- Pocket.
- 2D Offset.
- 2D Adaptive.

Those operations need their own wall-finish path. A Pocket must not repeat its complete area-clearing path as a spring pass.

2D Chamfer remains separate because its passes move a tool cone across a chamfer width. That work is tracked by #3238.

This issue does not add:

- A separate spindle speed.
- A separate feed for every pass.
- A second lead editor.
- A different finish tool.
- Automatic tool changes.
- Floor finishing.
- A new 3D finishing pass system.

A separate finish operation remains valid when the job needs another tool, spindle speed or different entry strategy.

## Documentation

Update the 2D Contour operation guide.

Document:

- The Passes controls.
- The finish-allowance formula.
- The difference between finishing and spring passes.
- The finish-feed override.
- Reuse of the existing lead settings.
- Safe retracts between offset bands.
- The one-operation workflow.
- The separate-operation workflow for a different tool.

Update the Pocket and Contour workflow. Keep the separate rough and finish operation method for jobs that use a different tool.

## Tests

Add focused tests for these cases:

- A disabled finish sequence produces the current toolpath byte for byte.
- One finishing pass consumes the complete finish allowance.
- Two finishing passes use the expected remaining allowance.
- Spring passes repeat the final offset.
- `Stock to leave` remains after the complete sequence.
- The same formula works for Inside and Outside contours.
- Open chains use the existing air-side classification for every pass.
- Multiple rings receive every required offset band.
- Multiple Z levels receive every required offset band.
- Keep-down links do not cross between offsets.
- Every offset uses the configured lead-in and lead-out.
- A fitting failure or collision on a later pass refuses the operation.
- Tabs remain valid for every pass.
- Control and wear compensation engage and cancel for every band.
- Finish feed inherits `Feed`.
- Enabling the override copies `Feed`.
- Editing `Feed` does not change an enabled override.
- Disabling the override restores inheritance.
- Lead-in feed uses the active rough or finish feed.
- Save and load preserve every setting.
- MCP create and update preserve every setting.
- UI edits stage and undo correctly.
- Spring passes remain present after post generation.

## Done means

- 2D Contour generates optional finishing and spring passes.
- Finishing passes divide `Finish allowance` correctly.
- Spring passes repeat the final wall path.
- Existing lead-in and lead-out settings control every pass.
- Finish feed can override the operation feed.
- Spindle speed remains unchanged.
- Unsafe later passes block posting.
- Existing operations retain current behavior.
- UI, project files, undo, MCP, posting, tests and documentation agree.

title: Stock STL export checks the f64 mesh, not the file: corners closer than one float32 step collapse as written; repair::weld keeps one of a back-to-back pair

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happened

`stock_export.rs` states the law "a hole is a refusal": the file must not claim a solid it is not. `machined_mesh` enforces it with `iso::unpaired_edges` (#4122) on the f64 triangles. `stl_bytes` then writes each corner as `f32`. Two corners closer than one float32 step are distinct in the checked mesh and one corner in the file. Their facets are written with a repeated corner, and the edges around them are no longer on exactly two facets. The check passed, but the file is not a closed solid.

One float32 step is 7.6 um at 64 mm, 15.3 um at 150 mm and 30.5 um at 300 mm, while the marching extractor places corners anywhere along a lattice edge. On a cut stock in our lane (31.7M facets, coordinates up to about 216 mm, cell 0.254 mm), the f64 mesh had 0 open and 0 unpaired edges. The file as written had 3 edges on three or more facets and 4 facets with a repeated corner, all at one spot, with corners 4 to 9 um apart where the step is 15 um.

A related gap in `repair::weld` (`crates/geometry`) matters for any fix that welds to the written values. `drop_degenerate` keeps the first of a set of duplicate facets. A closed mesh can weld into a back-to-back pair (the same three corners, opposite windings). Each of its edges is then on two facets of the pair, so dropping only one leaves those three edges odd: the weld opens the mesh it was meant to clean.

Measured on main e6849c5ae, synthetic, through the public `stock_export::stl_bytes` and `repair::weld`:

| Input (closed in f64: 0 open, 0 unpaired) | After | open | unpaired | repeated-corner facets |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tetrahedron near 150 mm, edge 0-1 split at a corner 3 um from corner 0 (6 facets) | `stl_bytes`, read back | 0 | 3 | 2 |
| thin tetrahedron: corners (150,150,150), (160,150,150) and two corners 3 um apart at (155,155,150) | `stl_bytes`, read back | 0 | 3 | 2 |
| the same thin tetrahedron | `repair::weld(.., 5e-6)`: kept 1, dropped 3 | 3 (`open_edge_count`) | | |

The closed answer for the thin tetrahedron is no facets at all.

### Steps to reproduce

1. The six facets: (p0, p2, a), (a, p2, p1), (p0, a, p3), (a, p1, p3), (p1, p2, p3), (p0, p3, p2), with p0 = (150, 150, 150), p1 = (160, 150, 150), p2 = (150, 160, 150), p3 = (150, 150, 160) and a = (150 + 3e-6, 150, 150).
2. `iso::unpaired_edges` is 0.
3. `stl_bytes`, then read the corners back as f32: `unpaired_edges` is 3, and 2 facets have a repeated corner.

Expected: the exported file passes the same closed check the export applied.

### Proposed fix

1. In the export, judge the mesh as it will be written. Round each corner to its `f32` value. When any facet collapses there, weld bit-exact on the rounded corners and drop the collapsed facets. Run `unpaired_edges` on that result, and write it or refuse by name. A mesh with nothing to collapse writes byte-identical to today.
2. In `repair::weld` / `drop_degenerate`, drop duplicate facets in pairs: k copies of one corner set keep k mod 2. A duplicate pair puts two uses on each of its edges, so dropping both keeps every other edge's count, and a closed mesh stays closed.

We use (1) in our own lane's writer, through `repair::weld` at 0. Pins: the two synthetic cases above (as written: closed after the fix), and a clean mesh writing byte-identical.

### Version and OS

main e6849c5ae (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`, `area:geometry`, `P3`.

body:
### What happened

`SdfField::subtract_batch` (`field_cut.rs`) refuses a chord whose clipped swept window adds more than `MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE` (1 << 22) cells beyond the tool at rest, and the message asks the caller to segment the move. Since #4079 the module law says segmenting always brings such a chord under the ceiling.

No caller in the crate segments. `simulate_field_with` (`backend.rs`, the field arm of `Stock::simulate`) and `Stock::simulate_undercut` (`field_undercut.rs`) pass each move whole, in chunks of `BATCH_MOVES` moves. So through the public `Stock` API, the field engine refuses ordinary moves that the column engine cuts, and the program has no field result at all.

Measured on main dc3679fb5, synthetic blocks, cell 0.254 mm:

| Move | Column | Field |
|---|---|---|
| 12.7 mm flat endmill, straight X pass 5 mm deep in a 30 mm block, 50 / 100 / 150 / 200 mm | cuts | cuts |
| the same, 300 mm | cuts | refused (the ceiling) |
| 127 mm flat tool, plunge 2 / 4 mm into a 200 x 200 x 30 mm block | cuts | cuts |
| the same, plunge 6 / 10 / 20 mm | cuts | refused |
| undercut disc head 127 mm across (height 3, neck 12.7 mm), plunge 2 / 4 mm (`simulate_undercut`) | (cuts nothing, by law) | cuts |
| the same, plunge 6 / 10 / 20 mm | | refused |

The ceiling is reached by the tool's footprint times its travel, so a wide tool reaches it in a few millimetres and an ordinary endmill on a long pass. A caller that segments by a fixed length still hits it: a 5 mm plunge of the 127 mm disc adds about 4.96M cells.

We found it in our own lane, which segments every move into 5 mm pieces before `simulate_undercut`: three programs with a 127.4 mm slitting disc plunging 15 to 28 mm were refused.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `Stock::block(Backend::Field { band: FIELD_BAND }, 0.0, 0.0, 340.0, 100.0, 30.0, 0.254)`.
2. `simulate` one feed move from (20, 50, 25) to (320, 50, 25) with a flat tool of radius 6.35.
3. The field engine returns `Err` (the ceiling). The same steps on `Backend::Column` return `Ok`.

Expected: both cut. The ceiling's own answer (segmenting) is applied by the simulator, not left to every caller.

### Proposed fix

In the field arm's callers (`simulate_field_with`, `simulate_undercut`, and the lathe and display arms that chunk the same way), split a chord whose work passes the ceiling into the fewest equal pieces that bring each under it, before `subtract_batch`. `subtract_batch` keeps its refusal as the per-update bound. The work of a straight chord grows with its length, so halving converges, and the number of pieces is bounded by the move's length in cells.

Pins: the steps above cut on both engines; the 6 mm plunge of the 127 mm disc cuts through `simulate_undercut`. The existing pin `a_wide_tools_long_chord_still_refuses_and_its_segments_cut` (from #4079, ours) moves to `subtract_batch` directly, where the refusal stays.

### Version and OS

main dc3679fb5 (source build), Windows 11.

### Labels

We cannot set labels. Our suggestion: `bug`, `area:sim`, `P3`.

title: Heidenhain posts: write the dialect of the control and NC software stated in the machine file

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
## Goal

HEIDENHAIN controls accept different program words per control and per NC software version. Today:
- the Klartext post accepts only iTNC 530 NC 340490-03;
- the DIN/ISO post writes words that are valid only on newer software (#4093, #4094).

The posts should read the control facts that the machine file already states and write the matching dialect. A control or version that a post cannot serve is refused by name.

## The machine file (no new field)

`controller.identity` already holds the facts (#3181, `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`):

```json
"controller": {
  "post": "Heidenhain Klartext",
  "identity": { "model": "iTNC 530", "nc_software": "340490-03", "installed_options": ["1", "19"] }
}
```

Proposal: keep the file to facts only. Make the values canonical:
- `model`: as HEIDENHAIN writes it (`TNC 320`, `iTNC 530`, `TNC 640`, `TNC7`, ...).
- `nc_software`: 6-digit ID, `-`, 2-digit release, optional ` SP<n>`.
- `installed_options`: HEIDENHAIN option numbers as strings.

A missing `installed_options` means "unknown": the post refuses or warns for functions that need an option.

## Capability flags (derived from model + NC software + options)

One shared resolver gives each post a flag set. The main flags, each with its HEIDENHAIN version source in the research notes:

- `language.iso`: DIN/ISO exists (none on TNC 124/128/310; TNC 320 from 340 55x-04; TNC 620 from 340 56x-02; TNC 426/430 from 280 472; TNC7 from 81762x-17).
- `blockForm`: `contour`, or `paraxial` for TNC 124/128 (one axis per block, no arcs): refuse.
- `decimals`: 3 (TNC 124/310/410) or 4.
- `toolCallByName`, `toolNameMax` (16, or 32 from TNC 640 34059x-02), `toolDefLR` (false on TNC7 from 81762x-19).
- `drill.c200` / `drill.c205`: the cycle parameter level. Q379/Q253 from iTNC 340 422. Q208/Q395 only from iTNC 60642x-04, TNC 640 34059x-04, TNC 620 81760x-01, TNC 320 77185x-05.
- `oldCycles`: cycles 1/2/17 definable, run-only (iTNC from 340 422) or absent.
- `preset.cycle247`: cycle 247 sets a datum value before iTNC 340 422, and activates a preset-table row after it.
- `dwell`: cycle 9 / `G04 F`, or `FUNCTION DWELL` (TNC 640 -07, TNC 620 -04, TNC 320 -04, TNC7; never on iTNC 530).
- `tilt` (none / cycle 19 / PLANE), `planeAxial`, `planeSym`; `tcpm.kt` / `tcpm.iso` (M128 or FUNCTION TCPM; ISO FUNCTION TCPM only from TNC 640 34059x-10 / TNC 620 81760x-07).
- `m140`, `m136m137`, `feedFzFu`, `arcs.spatial`, `arcs.helixLin`, `q.qs`, `q.qlqr`, `q.formulaPriority2020` (TNC 640 34059x-11: always write parentheses).
- Option gating: tilting needs option 8 (iTNC: 1), TCPM option 9 (iTNC: 2), and on TNC 620 cycles 201-205/208/209 need option 19.

The profile table (control and version range to flag values) is in the research notes. It covers TNC 310, 410, 426/430, iTNC 530 (four profiles), TNC 320, TNC 620, TNC 640 and TNC7.

## What the posts branch on

- **Klartext:** profile check (replaces the fixed 340490-03 check), tool call form, the `M140` retract or `L Z.. M91/M92`, cycle 247, dwell form, and later the drilling cycles and the cycle parameter level.
- **DIN/ISO:** refuse when `language.iso` is false; the G200/G205 parameter level; always `G04 F` for a dwell unless `FUNCTION DWELL` is confirmed for ISO programs; `G247` only with the preset-table meaning; the coordinate format.

## Scope and order

1. The resolver and flags in one place (post engine or a shared post helper), with a table test: control + version → flags.
2. The DIN/ISO post uses it for the fixes in #4093 and #4094 (these can land first with a narrow check, and move to the resolver here).
3. The Klartext post uses it, and serves more than 340490-03.
4. A refusal by name for an unknown model or version (no silent fallback, because cycle 247 changes meaning between versions).

## Done means

- The resolver maps each control/version in the profile table to its flags. A table test pins it.
- Both posts branch on the flags, not on fixed version strings.
- An unknown control or version is refused by name.
- The goldens of the shipped Picomax machine file do not change, except for the fixes of #4093 and #4094.

Source: HEIDENHAIN's public manuals and "Overview of New and Modified Software Functions" documents, collected and compared by the author's agent (notes, not in the repository). Related: #3095, #3181, #4085, #4086, #4087, #4088, #4093, #4094.

body:
## The maintainer's words

2026-11-25: "Well we need a unifying approach to this planning and it calls for a motion planning kernel that dictates how motion can be implemented"

## Problem

Strategies have their own pass planners, link code and entry code. The same selection can give rings in one strategy and straight slots in another. A fix in one planner does not reach the others. #3743 designed a shared ring planner for 2D. This issue makes that design one kernel with a contract.

## The pipeline

1. Region: selection (edge, face, chain, points joined by lines), material side, bounds.
2. Guide curves: rings (concentric or morphed), rows, medial lines.
3. Load control: none, trochoidal, constant engagement. It changes a guide curve.
4. Order: start side (inside or outside) and direction.
5. Link: stay at depth. Lift only with a named reason.
6. Entry and exit: air entry, pre-drilled hole, cleared column, helix, ramp, arc, plunge.

A strategy is a set of choices for these stages. A strategy has no planner of its own.

## Laws

- The same region and the same guide choice give the same curves.
- The material side and the start side are separate parameters.
- The start side changes only the order and the start point.
- A fallback is visible. The status line names it.
- An entry into material needs a proof. Else the kernel refuses with a reason.
- A cut above the engagement limit is prevented or named.
- A move that migrates keeps its output. A defect fix is a separate change.

## Names

Use "path kernel" (for example `crates/motion/src/path_kernel/`). "Kernel" already means the geometry kernel and a heavy lane.

## Order of the steps

1. K0, the design record. #3750 can start at the same time, because it keeps its output.
2. K1.
3. K4 (order and link) and K5 (entry and exit).
4. K3 (load control) and K6 (move the strategies).
5. K7 grows with each step.

## Sub-issues

| Step | Content | Issues |
|---|---|---|
| K0 | Design record: stage types, laws, scope | #4024 |
| K1 | Region model: selection, material side, bounds | #4025 |
| K2 | Guide curves | #3750, #3788 |
| K3 | Load control | #4026, #3932, #3933, #3849 |
| K4 | Order and link | #3750, #3757, #3758 |
| K5 | Entry and exit | #3746, #3934, #3759, #3397 |
| K6 | Move the strategies | #3752, #3753, #3754, #3755, #3756, #3760 |
| K7 | One test suite for the laws | #4027 |

## Related issues

- Start and exit picks (#3325, #3327, #3329) stay separate. They use the start point of K4.
- #3323 is `P?`. It is only linked here.
- #3743 and #3741 are the earlier research and report.

## Scope

2D milling comes first. Then the 3D Pocket levels. 3D finishing, multi-axis, turning, sheet and EDM are not in this issue.

## Done means

Each 2D milling strategy plans through the kernel. The K7 suite is green. No strategy has its own ring, link or entry code.

body:
Part of #3743. Builds on step 1 (#3750) and on #3744. Step 2 of the migration.

## The maintainer's words

#3741: "Where it should have just followed the contour keeping its plan not lifting the tool."

#3741 rule: "A lift is permitted only when an in-plane link would cut the part or a fixture. Then the status line names the reason."

## What happens

2D Pocket uses the same start-side planner as 2D Offset, with the dead-end ramps on (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs:314-318`, `ring_plan_ramped(..., true)`). Thus a Pocket with Pass starts at Inside or Outside has the defects of #3741: other rings for each start side, a lift at each piece, and the #3577 dead-end ramps.

Pocket Waterline and OffsetRings use a second planner (`waterscan.rs:62-216`, through `pocket_plan.rs:20-36`). Its rings are chained only where a chord is clear (`waterscan.rs:217`). Each other pass break lifts by the `Retract` pass link of `Links::PLANAR` (`crates/motion/src/links.rs:86-94`, `ladder_links.rs:163`), with no proof and no reason.

## Fix approach

1. 2D Pocket gets its rings from `ring_set` with `RingRef::Boundary` (the walls and the islands, Held 1991). Waterline, OffsetRings, Inside and Outside all use it. Pass starts at changes only the order of k and the start point.
2. The links between rings use `ring_links`. A lift has a named reason.
3. The entry uses `ring_entry`. A closed pocket has no air path, so the first entry is a pre-drilled hole, a cleared column, or the user's helix or ramp. A pocket that is open to the stock edge enters in air.
4. Remove the Pocket call of `ring_plan_ramped` and of `plan_passes` for the ring strategies.

## Pins

- `pocket_inside_and_outside_cut_the_same_rings`: on a square pocket with a round island, Inside, Outside and Waterline give the same multiset of rings (1 um, after a start-point and direction normalisation).
- `pocket_rings_do_not_lift`: the same pocket has 0 lifts on one level. Each lift on the fig8 pocket has a named reason.
- `pocket_has_no_dead_end_ramp`: no ramp along a pass on a start-side Pocket.
- Equivalence: the ring radii, the verifier verdicts and the gouge checks of `crates/app/tests/pocket_pass_start.rs` and `crates/motion/tests/rest2d.rs` do not change, except the lift counts and the entries that this issue fixes.

Effort `max`: a planner change under the safety floor. Priority P1: needless lifts and ramps into material in the posted program.

Done means: 2D Pocket rings come only from `ring_set`, the pins are green, and each lift has a reason on the status line.

title: STEP import removes a short edge from a Fusion solid and then refuses the enlarged gap

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
### What happens

CamCraft refuses a Fusion STEP model of a heater block. The user reproduced the failure in the desktop app on macOS (v0.24.0, commit `e6e04f5d0`). The MCP tool `import_model` gives the same result. Two AP214 exports and one AP242 export contain the same edge geometry. All three give this diagnostic:

```text
import_model: corrupt STEP: solidcore: import_step produced an invalid result: 1 of 1 solid item(s) refused; first #14 at check: a vertex sits 1.157e-2 mm off its edges (limit 1e-3) - re-export the model, or import an STL
```

The user can view an STL copy. A STEP copy exported from FreeCAD gives the same gap. The original CAD files stay local.

### Where the gap comes from

A diagnostic probe built the same STEP record twice with the pinned Solidcore version (`2016386`). Only the healing setting changed.

| Measurement | Before healing | After normal import healing |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Edges in the solid | 999 | 998 |
| Gap at the start of spline edge `#3375` | 0.006223 mm | 0.011573 mm |
| Largest vertex-to-endpoint gap in the solid | 0.007736 mm | 0.011573 mm |

The file defines edge `#3407` between vertices `#2564` and `#2120`. The vertices are 0.009944 mm apart. Spline edge `#3375` starts at `#2564`. Healing removes `#3407` and redirects `#3375` to `#2120`. Measuring from that vertex to the same spline endpoint reproduces the reported gap. The diagnostic names the solid (`#14`), so the user cannot identify the affected edge.

FreeCAD (Open CASCADE) keeps both vertices and all 999 edges. It reports one valid, closed solid with 345 faces. The file declares 0.010 mm uncertainty.

### Two limits still apply

The largest gap before healing already exceeds CamCraft's fixed 0.001 mm vertex limit. A separate probe passed the reader's record to the machining mesher at the normal 0.005 mm chord target. The mesher refused face 0 with a measured deviation of 0.011141 mm. Increasing the vertex limit alone would still leave a mesh refusal.

### Decision requested

Can the importer preserve an explicit short edge when collapsing it increases the endpoint error on an adjacent edge? If the preserved solid still exceeds machining tolerance, should CamCraft offer a reduced-fidelity view or refuse it with the measured accuracy? Issue #2976 and PR #2994 provide a precedent for reduced fidelity on an edge-to-surface gap. This case concerns a vertex and a curve endpoint.

**Done means:** A synthetic STEP regression fixture covers two distinct vertices joined by a short edge beside a spline. The test checks the edge count and the endpoint error before and after healing. A second test pins the agreed import outcome when the source exceeds machining tolerance. The user can see which check failed and the measured gap. Machining checks continue to use the accuracy the importer achieved.

**Triage.** P3 because direct STEP import fails and an STL copy works for viewing. `effort:high` because the fix changes geometry repair and needs a regression test.

[STEP build and validation](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/e6e04f5d0/crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step.rs#L297-L337) · [Vertex limit and measurement](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/e6e04f5d0/crates/kernel/src/solidcore_import.rs#L106-L157)

body:
Reported by flamingfire (Discord, relayed by the user, 2026-11-19), v0.24.0 (f2d78f31), Windows.

## What happens

Project `Rotor.camproj`: model `WVF350-101-453`, a long helical rotor (screw-compressor style lobes, shaft ends) laid along X; machine Doosan DNM 5700 + rotary table (A about X), Fanuc post; one 6 mm ball nose; a box stock around the part. Rotary Parallel1 (Source: Stock) and Rotary Contour1 both refuse:

```
generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: Rotary Parallel1: invalid machining parameters: the model's normals share no rotation axis - a turned workpiece is rotary work; finish a freeform with the 5-Axis kinds
```

The refusal is correct for today's design (the rotary operations fit the axis of revolution from the mesh normals, and a helicoid has no common axis). But this part is classic **4-axis wrap work**: it is clamped in the A axis on its own centreline, A turns and the tool follows the lobes. The user has a 4-axis machine, not a 5-axis one, so the message's advice ("finish a freeform with the 5-Axis kinds") does not help.

## Wanted

1. When the model is not a solid of revolution, the rotary operations can take the axis from the setup instead: the mounted machine's rotary line (A about X) through the WCS / a stated centre (e.g. the stock's or the shaft ends' fitted axis), stated by the user, not guessed.
2. Rotary Parallel (and Rotary Offset roughing) then wrap the toolpath round that axis with the existing radial field check (gouge against the fitted skin = the model itself, stock, part), so a helical rotor, auger, fluted shaft or cam with non-turned features can be finished on 4 axes.
3. Until then, the refusal message names the 4-axis case: e.g. "the model is not a shape of revolution; rotary operations need one today (#this). A part clamped on A that is not turned (helical lobes) is not supported yet" - not only the 5-axis pointer.

## Notes

- The shaft ends of this model are turned; only the lobes are helical. The ends alone would fit an axis, so "fit the axis from the turned faces only" could be a first step.
- Safety floor: the axis must be stated or fitted from real turned faces; a guessed axis that is off by a fraction of a mm wraps a gouge. Refuse when the stated axis and the turned faces disagree.
- Clean-room: published 4-axis wrapping literature only.

Done means: the reporter's kind of part (helical lobes between turned ends, on A about X) generates a Rotary Parallel finish that passes the radial gouge check and posts on the Doosan/Fanuc posts; a part with no turned faces and no stated axis is still refused, with a message that names the 4-axis case.

## What happens

Small drill-cycle readings from the QA run, checked on upstream main abe24ff09 (`crates/motion/src/drilling/hole.rs` `auto_kind`, `cycle.rs`):

1. **Auto counts the air above the hole as depth.** The auto law reads depth as R plane - bottom. With Top Z at top_of_model (z 15) and holes starting at z 10 and 7, a 3.5 mm spot (bottom z 6.5 / 3.5) reads as 8.5 / 11.5 mm deep and resolves to a chip-break peck: `G73 X8 Y8 Z-10.5 R-2 Q18 F300` (Q = 3 x d = 18, more than the whole depth). A 3.5 mm spot should be G81 (or G82 with a dwell).
2. **No way to ask for G83.** The `cycle` choices are auto, spot, drill, peck, tap, bore, back_bore, floating_tap, ream. `peck` is always the chip-break G73; the full-retract G83 (`CycleKind::Deep`) is reachable only through auto when depth > 4 x d. A user who wants full retracts in a deep or gummy hole cannot say so.
3. **The choices are not listed.** `list_operation_types` shows `cycle` as a string with default `auto`, without the allowed words, so an agent does not find `spot` (which exists and would have served the QA run's spot drilling, see #897).

## Expected

Auto measures depth from the hole's entry (or the material top over it), not from the R plane; an explicit full-retract choice (e.g. `deep`) posts G83; `list_operation_types` lists the cycle words.

Repro: **Part (p01-flange):** 6061 plate 100 x 60 x 10 mm centred on the origin (z 0..10), a 60 x 30 x 5 mm island on top (z 10..15, R5 corners) with a 1 x 45 deg chamfer on its top edges, 4 x dia 6 through holes at (+-42, +-22), a 10 mm wide x 3 mm deep slot across the +X end (x 35..45, floor z 7). Stock: box fitted to the model with +2 mm on top (100 x 60 x 17, z 0..17). WCS G54 at the stock's min-X min-Y top corner, world (-50, -30, 17). Machine Tormach 770MX, post Tormach PathPilot. Then a Drill with any tool on the detected holes, `cycle: "auto"`, a hole floor 3.5 mm below its entry; `post {post: "Tormach PathPilot"}`.

P7: the posted cycles are legal and cut the right depth; this is wording and choice.

Found by the QA swarm (SolidCraft v0.44.1 + CamCraft v0.23.0, part p01-flange). Re-checked on upstream main abe24ff09.

**Done means:** a 3.5 mm spot under a 5 mm air gap posts G81/G82 under auto; `cycle: "deep"` (or the chosen word) posts G83; `list_operation_types` lists the cycle words; tests pin each.

body:
Asked for by the user (2026-11-13, in chat): research-only issue for waterjet support, starting from the WAZER desktop waterjet the user owns. **Research, not code.** Pick never takes this issue; it is answered in comments and broken into sub-issues.

## Sources and clean-room rules

Clean-room rules for this research:
- **Used:** WAZER's public documentation (its support article on G-code and its materials and specs page; URLs below, cited, not copied), the Pro WAZER user manual (behaviour only), general abrasive-waterjet knowledge, and a behavioural analysis of the user's own job files exported by WAZER's web app (WAM). Those are about 120 programs from WAM 1.6 to 2.4, all Pro WAZER. Only their word and code usage and statistics were studied; no file is shared or committed.
- **Not used, and never to be used:** any Autodesk Fusion or HSMWorks post or output for WAZER (one exists in Autodesk's post library; it was not opened), WAM's JavaScript, and the machine's firmware.
- **Licence:** WAZER's G-code page is proprietary ("all rights reserved"). It is a published description of the dialect, not an open specification. Facts such as code numbers and meanings may be implemented; its text may not be copied.

## Findings so far

**Dialect** (WAM output, meanings as WAZER publishes them):
- **Modes:** G21 (mm) and G90 only. Moves are G0 and G1 only: **no arcs**, so curves are short segments. **No Z axis.** F is in mm/min. Dwell is `G4 S<seconds>`.
- **Jet and abrasive:** M3/M5 open and close the water, M8/M9 the abrasive.
- **Machine-specific M codes:** start and end of job (no M2/M30), the cut's bounding box (used by the machine's "check cut extents"), re-pierce time after a pause, and header metadata (WAM version, material name truncated to 20 characters, thickness, estimated time).
- **File format:** CRLF line endings, `;` comments, a fixed parameter header.
- **Origin:** top-left of the bed, Y negative toward the front. The cutting area is about 460 × 305 mm.
- **Per contour:** rapid to the pierce point, water on, abrasive on, stationary pierce dwell, straight lead-in, contour, then a short dwell, abrasive off, dwell, water off, dwell. The jet is never on during a rapid.
- **Kerf:** compensation is in the geometry (about half the published kerf), with no G41/G42.
- **Tabs** are uncut gaps (most contours are open).
- **Cut order:** inner contours first.
- **Feed:** the file's top F is the material rate for the chosen quality. The three qualities run at about 1 : 1.14 : 1.29. **Corner slowdown is written into F** in steps, down to about 0.45×.

**Machine:** kerf about 1.1 mm (0.044 in), maximum about 75 ipm; the pressure differs between the Pro and desktop models. The manual's error list includes a refusal of files generated by a much older WAM than the firmware.

**Materials and speeds:** the public page gives, per material and thickness, a cut rate and pierce time for each of the Pro and desktop machines. The published Pro rates sit near WAM's fine-to-medium rates; WAM's pierce times are often shorter than the published ones.

**Warranty and terms:** WAZER states that only WAM-generated files are approved, and that **edited or third-party-generated files void the warranty and breach its terms of service.** A community report says non-WAM files can leave uncut sections after pause and resume. Any CamCraft WAZER post must carry this warning prominently and must not claim WAZER approval.

## Open questions (answer before any sub-issue)

1. **Should CamCraft ship a WAZER post at all,** given the warranty and terms-of-service statement, or only a generic abrasive-waterjet post plus a user-supplied machine file? Decide with the maintainer.
2. **Pause and resume:** what does the firmware need for a third-party program to resume correctly (re-pierce after a pause, the bounding-box words)? Can that be learned from public docs alone?
3. **The corner-slowdown model:** derive it from public waterjet literature (taper and lag versus speed) rather than copying WAM's step table. What do the references say?
4. **Pierce data:** reuse #1521 (pierce and dwell data keyed by material and thickness), with waterjet as a process kind there?
5. **The operation:** a 2D abrasive-waterjet profile op, or a waterjet mode of the existing plasma/laser profile? Covers kerf offset in the geometry, leads on open contours, tabs as gaps, inner contours first, and arc linearisation tolerance.
6. **The machine file:** bed envelope and origin, kerf, max feed, model-specific speed tables (Pro vs desktop) and the bounding-box limit check.
7. **WAM project files (`.wzr`):** these are JSON with the source drawing and settings, undocumented. Importing them is out of scope unless WAZER documents the format; record that decision.

## Candidate sub-issues (filed only after the questions above are answered)

- Abrasive-waterjet profile operation (kerf, leads, tabs as gaps, inner-first order)
- Waterjet corner-slowdown and pierce-time model from published literature
- WAZER (Pro and desktop) machine definition and post, from the public dialect, with the warranty warning
- Waterjet process data in #1521's pierce and dwell tables

## Public references

- WAZER, "Understanding G-code": https://support.wazer.com/resources/preprocessing-temp/understanding-g-code
- WAZER materials and specs: https://wazer.com/materials/materials-specs/
- WAZER web app (WAM): https://wam.wazer.com/wazercam (a JavaScript app; no format docs without logging in)

Related: #1521 (plasma, laser and waterjet pierce and dwell data).

Done means: each open question is answered in a comment, the sub-issues are filed (one `P*`, one `effort:*`, `area:*`, `source:agent`, a Done means line and "Part of #<this>"), and this umbrella is closed with links to them.

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "We should be able to load DXF file to do profile cuts on."

What is missing: the importers read solid and mesh models only. A 2D drawing (a DXF from a CAD or sheet-metal program) cannot be loaded, so a flat part cannot be profiled without first being modelled as a solid. No DXF code exists in the tree today; issues 743 and 744 want DXF for tool and fixture profiles and can share this reader.

Wanted:
- A DXF reader for the 2D entities that carry a profile: LINE, ARC, CIRCLE, LWPOLYLINE and POLYLINE (with bulges), ELLIPSE and SPLINE (flattened within a tolerance, arcs kept as arcs where they are arcs). Units from `$INSUNITS`, with a question to the user when the file states none (never a silent guess between mm and inch). Layers are kept, so the user can pick by layer. Blocks/INSERT are expanded or refused by name; text, dimensions and hatches are skipped and counted in the import summary.
- The drawing loads as sketch geometry on the setup's XY plane: shown in the viewport, placed with the stock, saved in the project file.
- Chaining: touching entities are joined into chains within a tolerance; closed chains are told from open ones, and outer loops from holes.
- The 2D operations (2D Contour first; Pocket, Slot, Engrave and the plasma/laser profile operations after) take those chains as their geometry selection, with side (inside/outside) and direction per chain, exactly as they take model edges today.
- Loading is an undoable command with its MCP tool (Everything Is a Command; commands ship with an MCP tool). Model > Open offers `.dxf`, and so does the viewport drop of issue 1450.

Safety:
- The reader is an importer of untrusted files: malformed group codes, truncated files, NaN or huge coordinates, zero-length entities and self-intersecting loops give a clean error or a named skip, never a crash or a hang; it gets a fuzz test like the other importers.
- A gap wider than the chaining tolerance leaves an open chain that is shown as open; it is never closed silently, and an inside/outside cut on an open chain is refused by name.
- A flattened spline or ellipse stays within the stated tolerance of the drawn curve, pinned by a test, so the cut part is to size.
- Units are part of the result: the import summary states them, and a wrong-unit part (25.4 times too big or small) cannot happen without the user having answered the question.

Sources: the DXF format from Autodesk's published DXF reference (a public file-format document; format only), written from scratch or through a permissively licensed crate if one fits (a new dependency needs the maintainer's yes and a `docs/decisions/` entry). No DXF sample files taken from another product's install tree.

Scope note: this is larger than one PR. Suggested split when it is picked up: (1) reader + fuzz test in the geometry crate, (2) sketch entity, project file and viewport display, (3) chaining and selection in 2D Contour, (4) the other 2D operations.

Done means: a DXF with an outer rectangle, two circles and a slot made of lines and arcs loads, shows in the viewport and survives save/reopen; a 2D Contour picks the outer loop (outside) and the holes (inside) and posts a program whose golden CL matches the drawn sizes; a file with no units asks; an open chain is shown and refused for a side-compensated cut; a corrupt DXF gives a named error; the fuzz test runs; undo removes the drawing; the MCP tool loads a DXF headlessly.

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.
